Those are the linter's and were not reported as findings. After the edits the ### macOS wall is four short paragraphs, which removes that warning as a side effect of the F8 fix rather than as linter work; the other three warnings are untouched. found.issue: missing-spine. The page declares `type: how-to`, and wiki/page-types.md:108-116 gives that type action-title sections and numbered steps inside each. This page has neither: every heading is a noun or gerund label (`The scan and the plan`, `The download`, `Proving it works`, `Platform notes`) and there is not one ordered list on the page. It is a narrative account of what the installer does, in a shape a reader cannot follow along with.
found.fix: Owned by tracker task T9, which reshapes the page and absorbs a numbered procedure from another page. Not this run's edit: gotcha 8 forbids restructuring in review.
found.reason: A reader holding the installer cannot tell what to do first, or when the page expects them to act rather than read. The type is right (wiki/page-types.md:101 names this page as a how-to in the corpus, and tasks/docs/artifacts/T1.research.json confirms it); the shape it promises is absent.

found.reason: A reader landing from search read a description of the article instead of a statement of what installing gets them, and could not tell in one line whether this was the page for their platform.

detailed_review.score_reasoning: Baseline 10 - (F1 2 + F2 1 + F3 2 + F4 1 + F5 1 + F6 1 + F7 0.5 + F8 0.5) = 1, so the page graded FAIL on the absolute spine before this run. Two of those terms are 2-point structural defects: F1, the how-to page with no procedure in it, and F3, a prerequisites section that answers its own question for Mac readers and not for Windows readers. The remaining 5 points were spread across a missing abstract (F2 1), two described screens with no figure (F4 and F5, 1 each), the LLM carrying two names on one page (F6 1), a five-item verification checklist written as a comma run (F7 0.5) and two unreconciled sizes for the same machine (F8 0.5). After the fix, open penalty is F1 2 + F3 2 = 4, so 10 - 4 = 6 and the verdict is NEEDS_WORK. Delta is +5, and none of it comes from F1: that finding sits at 2 in both sums by design, because it is T9's work and grading it against T1's corrections would be dishonest in the other direction. The score is low for a page that reads well, and that is the spine working as specified: an absolute grade of the document as it stands, where one open 2-point defect is worth more than every sentence-level improvement combined. The linter could not be run in this session; its rules were hand-simulated from source instead and nothing it owns was scored, so the four long-paragraph warnings on this page cost the score nothing.
detailed_review.what_worked: The page now opens the way every type in wiki/page-types.md is supposed to: one sentence under the title that states what the reader gets, naming both platforms, before the overview paragraph (F2). The two screens a reader has to recognize, the plan card they approve and the final screen where they answer whether they heard Sulivan, now carry pending figures with capture instructions specific enough to shoot from (F4, F5). The LLM has one name on the page instead of two, which matters most in the verification section where a reader is matching the page against a screen (F6). That same verification section is now five checkable bullets instead of a five-clause sentence, which is the difference between reading it and using it (F7). And the two sizes the page prints for the same 8 GB Mac, 4.5 GB free disk and a 3.77 GB download, are reconciled in one clause traced to crates/hearth-probe/src/plan.rs:236-237, so a reader sizing a drive knows which number is theirs (F8). All six protected figures survived untouched, which was the point: 3.77 GB, 7.14 GB, 4.5 GB, 8.6 GB, 17,408 and 65,536 are the planner's byte counts under the product's own renderer, and the page agrees with the installer's screen. As a side effect of F8 the 130-word macOS wall became four short paragraphs, which is a linter warning cleared without a linter finding being filed.
detailed_review.what_holds_score_down: Both open items are 2-point structural findings, and neither is a sentence problem. F1: the page declares `type: how-to` and contains no numbered steps and no action-title headings, so a reader with the installer running has narrative where they need a procedure. That is T9's, and this review is forbidden from reshaping a page. F2 through F8 were all cheaper to fix precisely because the shape question was left alone. F3: `Before you start` gives a Mac reader four requirements and a Windows reader none, and forwards them to a page that describes the app after it is installed. That gap got slightly more visible after this run, not less, because the free-disk sentence now sizes the install for a Mac and still says nothing to the Windows reader who was told to point it `anywhere with room`. Nothing new was found at regrade. Two items too small to score are named below so they are not lost: the source line at wiki/installing.md:116 is wrapped past the corpus width, and `last_reviewed` still reads 2026-08-09 after two edit passes.
